analysis.title: Aerospace & Defense 3Q26 half-time report: Defense has been bought, aero sold; positioning ahead of mid-terms, oil outlook
key_insights: Across the large-cap A&D companies that have reported 3Q26, revenue beat consensus by an average of 2.4% and EPS by 3.6% (excluding the 119% EPS beat at SPCX). 15 companies in RBC coverage have reported.
Within RBC coverage, 73% of companies beat on revenue, 86% on margin, 79% on EPS and 86% on FCF.

Defense primes posted 3Q26 organic growth of about 10% and an average defense book-to-bill of 3.3x, with every prime above 1.0x. Every defense company beat on margin, EPS and FCF, and NOC was the only one to miss on revenue.

Defense stocks rose an average of 3.5% on the day of results and 4.4% over three days. RBC says expectations were low going in and that investors see the mid-terms as a clearing event, with a possible step-up in Iran war activity afterward.

RBC thinks some of the defense strength is being sold on November 2 as investors wait for the mid-term election results and a lower FY27 defense budget. It expects a ~$60B supplemental DoW funding bill before the new Congress and an FY27 base budget of about $1.1T, with limited growth beyond it. That creates crowding-out risk that keeps sentiment on the defense primes in check.
RBC continues to favor the defense tech names KRMN and MRCY. KRMN gives exposure to the urgent missiles and munitions restocking priority, and MRCY has execution upside and margin expansion.

Aerospace stocks fell an average of 2.3% on the day of results and 1.9% over three days. Aftermarket results were strong, with engine aftermarket growth of about 18% and component aftermarket up 8%, but did not beat elevated expectations or change the bearish 2027 growth narrative.
GE Aerospace reported total services growth of 17%, down from about 30% in 1H26. Safran reported spare parts sales growth of 17% against RBC's sense of investor expectations near 20%.

Higher crude prices remain an overhang for aerospace. RBC notes fleet indicators show minimal impact from higher jet fuel prices and roughly flat ASK growth, with no meaningful rise in parked aircraft or retirements.

The aerospace OE outlook softened as Boeing sounded more cautious on 737 MAX production rate increases. RBC attributes this mainly to internal MAX wing system integration issues and sees little risk to Airbus and Boeing backlogs, but investor confidence in backlog-to-cash timing has moved out.

3Q26 commercial deliveries across Airbus, Boeing and Embraer fell 1% y/y, while engine and component supplier revenues rose 22% and 21%. RBC does not see supplier de-stocking as a significant risk today but flags it as a 2027 watch item if deliveries keep disappointing.
RBC sees potential for suppliers to outperform until confidence in 2027-2028 Airbus and Boeing delivery growth improves.

Minimal downward 2026 guidance revisions across coverage. Boeing cut delivery estimates and gave out-year FCF guidance below consensus, and FTAI lowered adjusted FCF guidance to fund the FTAI Power ramp. All reporting defense companies raised 2026 guidance to some extent, while only GE and HWM among aerospace names raised meaningfully.

RBC favors VSEC for commercial aftermarket exposure, expecting a beat-and-raise quarter and a possible positive catalyst at the December investor day, where it expects medium-term guidance of about high-single-digit organic growth and 20%+ adjusted EBITDA margins.

RBC favors DPC for commercial OE exposure and IGT upside, and sees the roughly 4.5x EBITDA turn discount to HWM on 2027E as an attractive entry point. It expects the risk from GE's CPP acquisition (vertical integration) to be less than feared.

market_movers.rationale: RBC favors KRMN for exposure to the urgent missiles and munitions restocking priority within US defense strategy.
RBC likes MRCY for execution upside and margin expansion, with the outlook yet to include upside across several markets.
RBC expects a beat-and-raise quarter, upside from recent M&A integration, and a possible positive December investor day.
RBC favors DPC for commercial OE exposure and IGT upside, and sees a ~4.5x EBITDA turn discount to HWM on 2027E as an attractive entry point.
Boeing was cautious on the MAX production rate due to wing system integration, but RBC sees little backlog risk and some conservatism in the mid-term FCF outlook.
GE raised 2026 guidance on sales, margin, EPS and FCF, though services growth slowed to 17% from about 30% in 1H26.
Howmet raised 2026 guidance on sales, margin, EPS and FCF, and the stock rose 5.5% on the day of results.
Lockheed rose 7.0% on the day and 15.2% over three days after beating on EPS and FCF and raising guidance.
Northrop was the only defense name to miss on revenue (-0.2%) but rose 4.6% on the day and 8.2% over three days.
L3Harris beat on revenue, EPS and FCF, raised guidance, and rose 6.8% on the day.
General Dynamics beat on revenue by 6.2% and raised guidance, with only 2 trading days post-earnings.
RTX beat on revenue by 3.5% and raised 2026 guidance across sales, margin, EPS and FCF.
Arxis grew organic revenue 29% with a 4.3% revenue beat and raised sales and margin guidance.
FTAI rose 17.3% on the day, though it lowered adjusted FCF guidance to fund the FTAI Power ramp.
Hexcel fell 9.5% on the day after a 1.1% revenue miss and 96 bps margin shortfall.
Honeywell Aerospace beat on EPS by 35.1% and raised EPS guidance, but fell 9.6% on the day.
SpaceX grew revenue 150.6% with a 13.5% revenue beat and 118.8% margin beat, and rose 7.8% on the day.

sector_views.rationale: Results were strong and guidance was raised, but the mid-term elections and a FY27 base budget of about $1.1T with limited growth create crowding-out risk that keeps sentiment in check.
RBC favors KRMN and MRCY for munitions restocking exposure and execution and margin upside.
Aftermarket growth is strong and commentary is positive, but elevated expectations and 2027 deceleration concerns weigh on sentiment.
Boeing's cautious MAX tone softened the OE outlook, so RBC sees potential for suppliers to do better until confidence in 2027-2028 Airbus and Boeing delivery growth increases.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported results, across large-cap A&D names that have reported: revenue beat consensus by an average of 2.4% and EPS by 3.6% (excluding the SPCX EPS beat of 119%). RBC coverage beat rates: 73% on revenue, 86% on margin, 79% on EPS, 86% on FCF (15 companies reported).

Defense averages reported for 3Q26: revenue beat 2.9%, margin beat 143 bps, adjusted EPS beat 10.9%, FCF beat 53.1%, organic revenue growth 13.5% (reported as the Defense Average in Exhibit 1), 1-day return 3.5%, 3-day return 4.4%.
Aerospace averages reported for 3Q26: organic growth 14.9%, revenue beat 0.5%, margin beat 78 bps, adjusted EPS beat (2.7%), FCF beat 31.4%, 1-day return (2.3%), 3-day return (1.9%).

Boeing reported 3Q26: revenue beat 1.0%, margin miss of 70 bps, adjusted EPS miss of 36.0%, FCF beat 40.6%, stock down 10.7% on the day. It lowered delivery estimates for 2026 and gave out-year FCF guidance below consensus.

GE Aerospace reported 3Q26: revenue beat 3.2%, margin beat 104 bps, adjusted EPS miss of 10.7%, FCF miss of 7.3%, and total services growth of 17% (about 30% in 1H26). It raised 2026 guidance on sales, margin, EPS and FCF.
Safran reported 3Q26 spare parts sales growth of 17% versus RBC's sense of investor expectations of about 20%. Safran fell 9.9% on the day.
Lockheed Martin reported 3Q26: revenue beat 1.1%, EPS beat 6.0%, FCF beat 92.7%, and raised 2026 guidance on sales, EPS and FCF.
Northrop Grumman reported 3Q26: revenue miss of 0.2%, margin beat 60 bps, EPS beat 9.9%, FCF beat 16.5%.
SpaceX (SPCX) reported 3Q26 revenue growth of 150.6% with a 13.5% revenue beat, an adjusted EPS beat of 118.8% and FCF beat of 17.3%.
Commercial aftermarket organic growth in 3Q26 was about 18% for engines and 8% for components per RBC's tracker. Commercial OE supplier revenue rose 21% and propulsion OE revenue rose 22%.

VSEC has not yet reported. RBC expects a beat-and-raise quarter and a December investor day with medium-term guidance of about high-single-digit organic growth and 20%+ adjusted EBITDA margins (RBC estimate).

tension_points.bull_case: Defense primes beat on margin, EPS and FCF, posted a 3.3x book-to-bill, raised 2026 guidance, and expectations were low. Mid-terms could be a clearing event with a possible step-up in Iran war activity afterward.
tension_points.bear_case: A FY27 base budget near $1.1T with limited growth creates crowding-out risk that keeps sentiment in check, and some of the initial strength is being sold on November 2.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The U.S. mid-term election results and the size of the FY27 DoW budget, with a ~$60B supplemental expected before the new Congress.

tension_points.bull_case: Engine aftermarket grew about 18% and component aftermarket 8%, demand commentary is robust, and fleet indicators show minimal impact from higher jet fuel prices.
tension_points.bear_case: Results did not beat elevated expectations, growth is decelerating into 2027, and higher crude prices remain an overhang with demand destruction risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful increase in parked aircraft or retirements would undermine the aftermarket bull case.
